observations: F2a (Li galvanostatic profile) shows a first discharge plateau at ~1.05 V reaching ~1330 mAh/g and a first charge of ~870 mAh/g with a plateau near ~2.0 V [obs2]
F2b (Na galvanostatic profile) shows a first discharge of ~865 mAh/g with a plateau near ~0.15 V, a first charge of only ~470 mAh/g, and just ~60 mAh/g remaining by the 40th cycle [obs1]
F2c (Li cycling data) shows charge capacity of ~870 mAh/g at cycle 1 rising to ~1050 mAh/g around cycle ~17 and settling back to ~840 mAh/g by cycle 40, with coulombic efficiency ~96% [obs3]
F2d (Na cycling data) shows discharge capacity falling from ~870 mAh/g at cycle 1 to ~480 mAh/g at cycle 2 and further to ~70 mAh/g by cycle 40 [obs4]
reference_reasoning.proposition: Li/PCO holds onto ~840-870 mAh/g after 40 cycles at 0.1 C, essentially matching its initial reversible capacity of ~870 mAh/g [n7], whereas Na/PCO collapses from ~870 mAh/g on the first discharge to only ~70 mAh/g after 40 cycles at 0.1 C [n8]
reference_reasoning.assumption: The cycling conditions (0.1 C, 40 cycles, half-cell format) applied to the Li and Na cells are comparable enough that the sharply different capacity retention reflects how each ion interacts with the PCO electrode rather than a difference in test setup [writer inference]
reference_reasoning.open: These galvanostatic and cycling panels show that Li/PCO is stable and Na/PCO fades badly, but they do not by themselves identify why the same electrode material behaves so differently for the two ions [writer inference]
reference_reasoning.handoff: The next step inherits the established performance contrast: Li/PCO retains ~840-870 mAh/g over 40 cycles [n7] while Na/PCO fades to ~70 mAh/g over 40 cycles [n8], as the outcome requiring explanation

steps.question_v4: Taking the pore structure you characterised in step 1 as given, what does the evidence below show about how the material performs in service?

note: MatMech supplies which stretches are causal; our graph supplies the content. Every verdict is model against model.

reasoning: Step 1 shows the N2 adsorption/desorption isotherm has a hysteresis loop running from P/P0 ~0.5 to 1.0 with an uptake of ~110 cm3/g, which is the signature of a type IV isotherm [obs1]. The pore size distribution inset peaks at ~5.5 nm and ~6.9 nm with a tail below 4 nm, pinning the dominant pore population in the mesopore range [obs2]. SEM shows agglomerated faceted particles of ~250-500 nm with open gaps between them, though the internal mesopores themselves are not resolved at that magnification [obs3]. Together these establish that PCO is mesoporous, showing a hysteretic type IV isotherm with pores mostly 5-7 nm [n5]. Step 2 takes this pore structure as given and turns to how the material performs in service [writer inference]. For the Li cell, the 1st discharge shows a long plateau near ~1.05 V reaching ~1330 mAh/g, and the 1st charge reaches ~870 mAh/g with a plateau near ~2.0 V [obs2]. Over subsequent cycling the Li charge capacity starts at ~870 mAh/g (cycle 1), rises to ~1050 mAh/g by about cycle 17, and settles back to ~840 mAh/g by cycle 40, with coulombic efficiency around 96% [obs3]. These data establish that Li/PCO keeps ~840-870 mAh/g after 40 cycles at 0.1 C, with an initial reversible capacity of ~870 mAh/g [n7]. For the Na cell, the 1st discharge reaches ~865 mAh/g with a plateau near ~0.15 V, but the 1st charge only reaches ~470 mAh/g, and by the 40th cycle capacity has fallen to ~60 mAh/g [obs1]. The cycling curve confirms this collapse, dropping from ~870 mAh/g (cycle 1) to ~480 mAh/g (cycle 2) and down to ~70 mAh/g by cycle 40 [obs4]. These data establish that Na/PCO fades from ~870 mAh/g (1st discharge) to ~70 mAh/g after 40 cycles at 0.1 C [n8].
end_to_end.why_weakest: Step 2 is framed as building on the pore structure established in step 1, but none of its cited observations (obs1-obs4, all voltage/capacity cycling data) reference porosity, pore size, or the isotherm at all, so the link between the mesoporous structure and the Li-vs-Na performance divergence is asserted rather than shown by the cited evidence.
